title: Sync admission: read (open=anyone / closed=roster) and write (ALWAYS roster) are ORTHOGONAL; capability decided per-connection and enforced in-session
body:
Product requirement (user, 2026-07). Openness and write-authorization are ORTHOGONAL axes — NOT a single open/private switch:

- READ admission (open/closed axis): an OPEN project commits its identifier into a CHECKED-IN `rag-rat.sync.toml` (distinct from the machine-local, gitignored `rag-rat.toml`); any peer with it downloads read-only with NO pairing. A CLOSED project serves reads only to its roster.
- WRITE admission is ALWAYS roster-gated, open AND closed alike. Invite-token pairing grants roster membership in both kinds; an open project merely ADDITIONALLY permits anonymous read. Matrix: open={read: anyone, write: roster}; closed={read: roster, write: roster} — differ only on the read axis.

THREE-LEVEL ROLE (selectable at enroll, default least-privilege). `DeviceRole` grows `{Member,Owner}` → `{ReadOnly, Writer, Owner}`: read-only (default) = read/sync only; writer = +write content; owner = +enroll devices. The per-connection CAPABILITY derives from role — anonymous downloader AND read-only roster device both → read-only; writer/owner → read-write; only owner runs enrollment. Enforcement is two-layer: FOLD backstop (a read-only/off-roster device's pushed entries carry no content authority → fold-rejected, the durable guarantee) + IN-SESSION gate (read-only peer's push frames refused at the wire; `run_session` is symmetric today with no per-peer capability — this gate is net-new). A read-only joiner still gets content KEYS (#763 catch-up) — read-only gates write, not decrypt.

TOPOLOGY (user's model): author + peer are the SAME level (full P2P devices); `serve` is an OPTIONAL stateful store-and-forward hub, never a required party, never owner authority. Enrollment is a P2P moment — the owner (author) device enrolls the joiner directly (ticket carries the owner's node addr); serve is uninvolved. AUTO-DISCOVERY between online peers is DEFERRED but must be stubbed: leave a documented `discover_peers(account_id) -> Vec<EndpointAddr>` seam (explicit-config impl today, relay-side account-keyed discovery later — mirrors held's discovery-node ALPN), so the device-sync driver just iterates the resolver's output.

Chosen internal defaults: custom canonical-CBOR ticket `{account_id, node addr, token, expiry}` (not iroh EndpointTicket); dedicated enrollment ALPN `rag-rat/enroll/1`; auto-enroll on redemption (token IS the approval; `sync init --role --label`); `sync open` generates `rag-rat.sync.toml {account_id,node_id,relay_url,open,name?}`. The account id is content-derived from genesis → self-certifying, so a downloader verifies everything cryptographically and the committed node id only says WHERE to look. Enrollment authoring (`DeviceAdd`) is OWNER-only and has NO production seam yet (test-only `pub(super)`); #763 key catch-up requires the target already roster-effective (enroll → fold effective → then catch-up). Full design: `pairing-and-open-projects-design.md`. See [[rag-rat-sync-content-alpn-dispatch]] and the node-auth memories.

title: candidate_capacity own-account exemption needs AUTHORING-TIME provenance, not roster membership (#884→#888)
body:
`candidate_capacity` (this file) applies the §18b remote-flood caps (4,096/author, 16,384 global) to `/3` content ingest. Own-account content (the account's own memories, from any of its devices) should be exempt from these caps — otherwise a same-account restore larger than the caps stalls (#884). BUT this is NOT correctly solvable with a roster-membership check at the ingest budget layer, and a naive attempt was reverted:

- Keying the exemption/exclusion on CURRENT membership (`account_roster_history ... closed_at IS NULL`) truncates the historical content of a device REMOVED before the restore (normal device-removal history) — the restore drops the tail.
- Keying it on EVER-membership (retain closed rows) lets a REVOKED device flood: its key still resolves against an old roster ref, so post-removal content is exempted forever.

Distinguishing "authored while an effective member" from "submitted after removal" is the authoring-time authority question the acceptance fold owns and candidate_capacity deliberately defers (#652). The correct fix is a per-row `own_account` provenance flag on `content_entries`, set at `insert_candidate` from the verified authoring authority (NEVER from the attacker-settable `author_account_id` — see the sibling SecurityNote), with the exemption admitting own-account entries uncapped and the counts excluding `own_account = 1`. Schema migration + backfill hook. Tracked in #888; lands with foreign-account ingest (#407) that makes the counts live.

Until then candidate_capacity keeps its pre-#884 local-device-only exclusion (`WHERE device_fingerprint != ?local_fp OR ?local_fp IS NULL`) — do NOT re-add a roster-membership check thinking it fixes #884; it does not, and it adds a hot-path read plus a P1 either way. This only bites at >16,384-memory accounts (real usage ~330), so the incompleteness is latent. Related: the exemption entry point for content sync is `OplogContentSyncStore` in crates/rag-rat-sync/src/store.rs.

title: Active embedding model is seeded from config on a fresh index — it does NOT default to embedding-hash (#394)
body:
BUG (#394) + fix. `active_embedding_model_id(conn)` (index/ai/helpers.rs) falls back to `HASH_MODEL_ID` when the `active_embedding_model` meta is UNSET, and nothing seeded it from config — so a fresh index silently used `embedding-hash` regardless of `[llm.embedding] model`, and `reconcile` blocked naming `embedding-hash` instead of the configured model. `EmbeddingBackend::default()` is all-MiniLM, NEVER hash.

FIX: `seed_active_embedding_model(conn, configured_model_id)` (index/ai/reconcile/model_lifecycle.rs) activates `config.llm.embedding.backend.model_id()` when a seed is owed. Called from every config-aware open: `rebuild` + `index_incremental_with_progress` (both INSIDE their txn — see atomicity), `open_config`, and `try_open_config_read_only` (returns None when a seed is owed → read-only tools fall back to the healing write path).

SEED-OWED = PROVENANCE, NOT A PROXY (load-bearing lesson). Don't infer "was the active model a user choice?" from `ai_models.installed` (a recovered cache is installed too) or `current_embedding_count` (explicit install has 0 embeddings pre-reconcile, AND it's an O(index) scan every open). RECORD it: `ACTIVE_EMBEDDING_MODEL_PROVISIONAL_META` ("active_embedding_model_provisional") = "1" AUTOMATIC / "0" or absent EXPLICIT|CONFIRMED. `activate_model_with_version(conn, id, version, provisional)` is the SINGLE writer stamping model+version+provenance together — `install_model` false (explicit), `recover_cached_fastembed_model` + the seed true (automatic). A reconcile committing embeddings (`embed_loop.rs`, `report.embeddings_written > 0`) calls `clear_active_embedding_model_provisional` → confirmed. `active_embedding_model_seed_owed`: model selected ⇒ owed when active unset OR (active != config AND `active_embedding_model_is_provisional`) — O(1). Absent flag ⇒ non-provisional ⇒ respected (pre-#394 indexes + explicit/committed models safe). One signal: explicit install sticks before first reconcile; recovered cache yields to config; config edit before install adopted; committed model never clobbered; no per-open scan.

EMBEDDINGS-OFF SYMMETRY (config `model="none"`, model_id()==None): reconcile/status are config-BLIND (`reconcile_with_options_progress`/`status.rs` read `active_embedding_model_id` from the active meta, NOT config; the CLI reconcile cmd does NOT gate on config=None), so the SEED is the ONLY config→meta bridge — disabling must flow through it too. `seed_owed(None)` owes a write only to CLEAR a still-active PROVISIONAL model (explicit/confirmed preserved) → `clear_active_embedding_model` drops model id + freshness version + provenance flag + remote config, so `active_embedding_model_id` returns to the hash fallback and nothing stale lingers. Restores the "embeddings-off ⇒ active unset" invariant; without it a repo first opened with a real embedder then switched to `none` keeps prompting for the disabled model. `delete_meta` is the index_meta counterpart of `clear_reconcile_meta` (`clear_active_remote_config` now builds on it).

TWO GAPS THE SEED SHARED WITH install (fix both when touching activation): (1) the seed clears `active_remote_config` (like `install_model`'s local branch) — else a reseed away from a remote activation lets `active_embedder` build an `OpenAiEmbedder` against the STALE endpoint → vectors in the wrong embedding space. (2) ATOMICITY — BOTH write-path seeds run INSIDE their transaction, never autocommit-before-BEGIN (a failed pass would otherwise strand the active model on a newly configured MISSING model, losing the old fallback): the `rebuild` seed before COMMIT (after set_meta indexed_at_ms); the `index_incremental_with_progress` seed inside its BEGIN IMMEDIATE block, folded into the `mutated` flag so a heal COMMITs while an idle pass with no heal owed stays a no-op read (preserves the #63 no-write invariant).

Seeding does NOT install — reconcile still BLOCKS until the configured model is installed — but the block message (`embed_loop.rs` / `status.rs`) names the CONFIGURED model.

TEST FOOTGUN: schema_bootstrap tests use `embedding-hash` as the no-download test embedder and used to rely on active-defaults-to-hash. A fresh index now adopts the CONFIGURED model, so a test that installs/uses hash must SELECT it (`config.llm.embedding.backend = HASH_MODEL_ID.parse().unwrap()` before `rebuild`): fixed `reconcile_requires_explicit_model_install_and_ignores_stale_artifacts`, `full_rebuild_preserves_installed_model_manifest`. Provenance unit tests (in-memory conn): respects_an_explicitly_installed_model, config_wins_over_a_provisionally_recovered_model, reseeds_a_provisional_model_when_the_config_changes, a_confirmed_model_is_respected_over_a_config_change, embeddings_off_clears_a_provisional_active_model, embeddings_off_preserves_an_explicit_active_model, embeddings_off_leaves_the_active_model_unset. Integration: reconcile_confirms_a_provisional_model_against_a_config_change; an_incremental_pass_heals_a_missing_active_model_atomically. `activate_model_with_version_writes_all_metas` asserts the provenance meta. PR #395.

title: Test HTTP stubs: macOS/BSD accept() inherits the listener's O_NONBLOCK → force blocking or large bodies truncate (#446)
body:
CROSS-PLATFORM TEST-HARNESS FOOTGUNS (#446) in the in-process HTTP stubs (embed_loop.rs `spawn_reconcile_embed_stub`/`spawn_selective_failure_embed_stub`; openai.rs `spawn_stub`/`spawn_body_capture_stub` + the concurrency stub). TWO distinct Windows/macOS socket bugs, both surfacing only on requests too big for ONE TCP segment:

1) macOS/BSD accept() INHERITS the listener's O_NONBLOCK (Linux/Windows do NOT — accept yields a blocking socket). The reconcile stubs `set_nonblocking(true)` for a poll-accept loop; the accepted socket is then non-blocking on macOS, so `set_read_timeout` (SO_RCVTIMEO) is a NO-OP and `read()` returns `WouldBlock` the instant no bytes are buffered. `read_request_body` treats `Err(_)` (incl. WouldBlock) as `break`, so a multi-segment body TRUNCATES → stub returns too few embeddings → reconcile batch fails the count check → `embeddings_written: 0`. FIX: `stream.set_nonblocking(false).ok();` at the TOP of `read_request_body`, before `set_read_timeout`. Tripped `remote_reconcile_chunks_large_selection_below_sqlite_bind_limit` (1005 chunks, one 4096-batch request); 4-item stub tests fit one segment and never saw it.

2) Windows abortive (RST) close on unread request bytes. openai.rs `spawn_stub` accepts, calls `drain_request` (originally a SINGLE `read`), writes the response, then DROPS the stream. On Windows a request can arrive in multiple segments, so one read leaves the tail in the recv buffer — and closing a socket with unread RECEIVED data is an ABORTIVE (RST) close there, which the client (ureq) surfaces as a transport error INSTEAD of the HTTP response. So `embed_batch_errors_on_{dim_mismatch,count_mismatch,http_500}` got a connection error, and their assertions on the error message ("512"/"3"/"http status 500"/"boom") failed. The happy-path test uses the same stub and passed only because its request landed in one segment — LOAD-DEPENDENT flaky, not deterministic. FIX: `drain_request` now delegates to `read_request_body` (full headers + Content-Length drain), leaving the recv buffer empty so the drop is a graceful FIN and the client reads the full response.

RULE for any in-process test HTTP stub: (a) if the listener is non-blocking, reset each accepted socket to blocking before a timeout-governed read; (b) FULLY consume the request (Content-Length body), never a one-shot read, before responding+closing — a partial drain triggers Windows RST-on-close. (rusqlite is `bundled`, so SQLite `SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER` is identical across platforms — the "below_sqlite_bind_limit" 1005-vs-999 theory is a RED HERRING; the cause is always the socket.)

title: #427: same-identity checkouts share ONE scope by design; index only warns (never re-scopes), plus a zero-file hard error
body:
Issue #427 asked whether an explicit-config `rag-rat index` of a linked worktree / same-identity clone SHOULD adopt the primary checkout's `source_root` + files. Decision (user-confirmed): **keep the A7 identity semantics unchanged** — `resolve_repo_identity` derives the SAME portable `repo_id` for the primary checkout, its linked worktrees, and any fresh `git clone`, so `register_repo` folds them into ONE scoped row-set. Load-bearing, not a bug. The fix is to make it LOUD, not to re-scope.

**Two loud-adoption warnings** (`crates/rag-rat-cli/src/commands/index_ops.rs::surface_adoption_warnings`, on BOTH one-shot and `--watch` paths, NOT `--worktree` overlays): (1) worktree re-anchor — `config.source_root_reanchored_from.is_some()`, see [[mem_19f374e0156_7f96768c59d6]]; (2) same-identity join — `same_identity_join_note(config)`.

**Empty-index invariant — enforce BEFORE adoption records the root, at the two INDEXING entry points, each OPEN+MIGRATE then check.** `index_incremental_with_progress` (incremental.rs): `open_bare(AdoptionPending)` (migrates) → `is_first_time_empty_conn(conn, config)?` → `adopt_repo_from_config`. `rebuild_with_progress` (rebuild.rs) SPLIT around `create_or_migrate`: PHASE 1 (fresh DB `!db.exists()`) refuses would-discover-nothing pre-create (no stray file, the `maintenance` contract); PHASE 2 (existing DB) refuses `is_first_time_empty_conn` post-migrate (a pre-registry/older DB is unreadable until migrated). `--allow-empty` (`Config::allow_empty`) opts in.

**ROOT-RECORDING IS INTENT-GATED (the same-identity-clone-prune fix, register_repo now has TWO public entries).** `schema::register_repo` (records the working-tree root in `repo_roots`) vs `schema::register_repo_read_only` (registers identity, records NO root) — both delegate to `register_repo_inner(.., record_root)`; `record_root` gates ONLY the `repo_roots` INSERT (idempotent path, adoption txn, and `merge_local_incumbent_into_registered`), every identity decision is identical. `adopt_repo_from_config(config, AdoptIntent)` (lifecycle.rs) picks: `AdoptIntent::Indexing` (rebuild/incremental/generation_rebuild test) → `register_repo`; `AdoptIntent::ReadOnly` (`open_config`: doctor/MCP/query) → `register_repo_read_only`. WHY: a recorded root is the "this checkout was INDEXED here" signal, so a mere READ must not create one (else a `doctor`/MCP read of a fresh same-identity clone makes it look indexed → a later empty index prunes the shared scope). `consolidate` uses `register_repo` (imports an indexed repo). The 63 direct `register_repo(4-arg)` test callers are unchanged.

**ONE recognition helper, INDEXING-ONLY signals (adoption_hints.rs `repo_indexed_at_this_root`), shared by the empty-index guard AND `same_identity_join_note`.** Two signals, either proves an indexing pass ran at THIS checkout: (1) PRIMARY — `schema::repo_has_recorded_root(repo_id, root)`; recording is now indexing-only, so this is immune to a read-only open AND to a same-identity SIBLING clone stealing recognition (each checkout records its OWN `repo_roots` row, so B indexing the shared repo leaves A's row intact). (2) FALLBACK — persisted `repo_meta[repo_id][source_root] == root`, for an identity-less (non-git/unborn) root that never gets a `repo_roots` entry (`adopt_repo_from_config` sole-picks WITHOUT `register_repo`). The single-valued `source_root` alone was WRONG: last-writer-wins, so a sibling clone's index overwrote it and made the earlier checkout look un-indexed → its empty prune got refused (#427 review "Preserve pruning for earlier same-identity checkouts"). `is_root_already_indexed[_conn]`: resolve repo_id → `repo_indexed_at_this_root`; PLUS a sole-placeholder fallback (`!multiple_real_repos && sole_repo_id`) for a legacy pre-adoption index. `is_first_time_empty[_conn]` = `!is_root_already_indexed && !would_discover_any_file` (`&&` short-circuits the walk).

`open_ro_compatible` (the SELF-opening probe) accepts a migrateable `Older` schema ONLY once `schema::table_exists(conn,"repos")` (the registry was ADDED in V038; probes run BEFORE the write-open migration, so a pre-V038 `Older` DB has no `repos` table and would fault `no such table: repos`).

Callers REACT to the typed `EmptyIndexRefused` (never re-derive): one-shot `index` surfaces it; watcher `run_pass`/`shutdown_discover` and `maintenance` `downcast_ref` → defer. **No-watchable-target `--watch` errors at STARTUP** — `run_watch` refuses `!config.allow_empty && config.target_directories().is_empty()` (keyed on `target_directories()`, not `targets.is_empty()`: a target with an empty dir list watches nothing).

Default SAFE: an indexing caller inherits the refusal; a read-open can't smuggle an empty scope. Index a clone/worktree as its OWN repo by pinning `[index] repo_id`. Tests: index_guards.rs (refuses_zero, allows_already_indexed_to_go_empty, discover_refuses_first_time_empty_against_existing_db, full_rebuild_prunes_existing_placeholder, maintenance_defers, watch_on_no_target/empty_target_dirs_errors, watch_with_targets_but_no_files_defers) + adoption_hints.rs (a_sibling_index_does_not_steal_an_earlier_checkouts_prune_right, a_read_only_open_does_not_make_an_unindexed_repo_look_indexed, same_identity_join_warns_even_after_a_read_only_open_of_the_clone, recognizes_non_git/legacy_placeholder, pre_registry_no_fault, tracks_indexing_not_shared_identity) + watch.rs maintenance_pass_defers.

**REBASED onto #460 (`0ee6562`, gix 0.85 / incremental-churn work). PR #458.** History squashed: commit `9b8657d` = the whole #427 empty-index + warnings work; a follow-up commit = the intent-gated root-recording + recognition rework above. The pre-#460 review-iteration commits (3434518/c8c71e0/5d5ebbe/31a36f3/68b443c + the superseded leaf-patch ones) were collapsed by the rebase.

KNOWN COSMETIC EDGE (defer): an explicit `--config` naming a linked-worktree absolute path against a shared DB with main already indexed trips BOTH warnings — `anchor_root_to_main_worktree` returns `main_root.join("")` → trailing slash so the re-anchored root no longer string-matches the recorded root. Registry helpers reused via [[mem_19f372f8d6c_9c541381eb09]].

title: Clone-graph treadmill: global content_revision gate rebuilds the full generation every watcher pass under continuous edits (~1 GB writes/pass)
body:
MEASURED (2026-07-07, `rag-rat mcp` serving this repo, agent editing continuously): 242 GB write_bytes / 470 GB rchar in ~6 h; one watcher pass = ~4.8 GB written, ~9.5 GB read, ~4.5 min; `clone_graph_generations.generation` counter reached 324 in that window (≈1 full generation per ~64 s while edits land).

MECHANISM: `pending_clone_graph()` gates freshness on `live.source_revision != content_revision()` — a GLOBAL digest over every indexed file. Any edit anywhere flips it, so every watcher pass tail (`watch.rs::run_pass`) spends leftover budget in `reconcile_clone_edges_pass`. Phase 1 there DISCARDS a Building generation whose `source_revision` no longer matches (CASCADE drops its edges/postings) and restarts from symbol 0. Under a continuously-editing agent the graph is rebuilt from scratch every pass: a Complete generation on this corpus is ~155k `clone_edges` + ~220k `clone_subblock_postings` (~100 MB of table+index rows), and each cycle pays INSERT of the new generation + DELETE of the old one, doubled again by WAL + checkpoint. A budget-tripped Partial generation (e.g. 93k edges) is pure waste — discarded next pass because the revision moved again.

The design assumed hook-driven cadence (rebuild after commit, then idle). An agent editing every few seconds turned it into a treadmill that never converged and dominated disk I/O.

STATUS: mitigated by the #472 quiet-window gate (PR #475): `IndexDatabase::clone_graph_rebuild_due` (precompute.rs) defers the background rebuild until `content_revision()` has been stable for `watch::CLONE_GRAPH_QUIET_MS` (5 min), shared by the watcher and CLI maintenance tails via per-repo meta (`clone_graph_quiet_*` keys). Explicit `clones --precompute` / full `index` stay immediate. The ROOT fix — incremental delta maintenance so small edits never trigger full rebuilds — is #473 (design in the issue): edges are df-independent verification results, prefix filtering is lossless under any single frozen token order, so per-changed-file deltas against the persisted postings are sound. Do NOT "fix" further by relaxing the exact-freshness eligibility of the postings fast path (see the CloneCorpus R1 memory).

title: chunks.embedding_policy freshness model: single writer chain, hardcoded-DEFAULT cap stamp, and the files.generated trap
body:
Facts that constrain any design that trusts the persisted `chunks.embedding_policy` column (e.g. a version-stamped GROUP BY fast path for the skip summary, #530):

1. SINGLE WRITER CHAIN: `chunks.embedding_policy` is written only by `prepare_chunks` (prep.rs) -> `insert_prepared_file` -> `insert_chunks` (file_index.rs). Full rebuild, incremental, and the heal path (post-#518/#552, via `prepare_index_content_from_text` -> `insert_prepared_file`) all route through it. `chunk_embeddings.embedding_policy` (ai/store.rs) is a SECOND, independent copy stamped at embed time with `LowSignalCheck::FromText` — it can legitimately differ from the chunks-table value (FromSpan) for chunks slicing into long comments/strings.

2. CAP INCONSISTENCY: `prepare_chunks` stamps the column at hardcoded `ai::DEFAULT_MAX_EMBEDDING_CHARS` (prep.rs) even though `max_embedding_chars` is user-configurable in rag-rat.toml (config.rs `RuntimeAiConfig`). `status.rs` calls `embedding_policy_skip_summary(conn, DEFAULT_MAX_EMBEDDING_CHARS)` unconditionally while `reconcile_with_options_progress` passes the runtime cap — so for a non-default-cap user, status and reconcile skip summaries ALREADY disagree today (SkipTooLarge/truncation only).

3. THE files.generated TRAP: the policy's generated gate reads `file_kind` (the stored `files.kind` from the target config) plus its own `looks_generated_path` — NOT the healed `files.generated` flag. `ensure_generated_flags_current` rewrites `files.generated` on write-bearing opens WITHOUT touching chunks. If anyone "unifies" the policy's generated gate onto `files.generated` (a tempting cleanup per the #202 decision memory), any persisted-policy fast path silently desyncs, because flag heals don't restamp chunk policies.

4. POLICY BEHAVIOR SURFACE is wider than `embedding_policy_for_chunk`: `cheap_skip_policy`, `MIN_EMBEDDING_CHARS`, `looks_generated_path`, `is_test_fixture_path`, `Language::supports_embeddings`, `is_plumbing_node`/`span_is_plumbing`, and the tree-sitter GRAMMAR CRATE VERSIONS (a grammar bump changes low-signal node kinds with zero rag-rat source change). A hand-bumped policy-version const cannot cover grammar bumps even in principle; only a behavior-corpus tripwire test (hash policy decisions over fixture snippets that really parse) catches those.

5. SCOPE: the skip summary's recompute joins `chunks JOIN files JOIN chunk_text` where `files` is the temp scope VIEW (repo + live generation). Bare `chunks` contains dead-generation rows and other repos' rows in a shared DB; any GROUP BY replacement must keep the identical FROM/JOIN. Note the chunk_text JOIN also silently excludes chunks lacking a chunk_text row.

title: V086 content_digest triggers own content_revision: files writers must register the fold; a files-table rebuild must ensure_content_digest + reseed
body:
The incrementally-maintained `content_revision` (#828, schema V086) is kept correct by three `AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE` triggers on `files` (`files_content_digest_ai/ad/au`) that call the registered DETERMINISTIC scalar `rr_content_digest_fold`. Two footguns for future work:

(1) EVERY connection that writes `files` rows MUST call `content_digest::register_content_digest_fold(conn)` first. Production opens do it in `IndexConnection::open` (storage.rs); `schema::apply` and `schema::migrate_forward` register it up front for raw test connections that apply the real schema then write `files`. A writer WITHOUT the function registered fails the `files` write with `no such function: rr_content_digest_fold` and ROLLS BACK — fail-closed BY DESIGN: a silent no-op would drift the digest under version skew. If you open a bare `rusqlite::Connection` and write `files`, register the fold.

(2) A files-table REBUILD migration (the `CREATE files_new … / copy / DROP TABLE files / ALTER … RENAME` pattern used by V040/V043) SILENTLY DROPS the triggers — they are objects ON the dropped table. Such a migration MUST call `content_digest::ensure_content_digest(conn)` again (recreates table+triggers, idempotent) AND reseed `content_digest_state`, or every subsequent `files` write drifts the digest with no error.

Backstop only: `verify_content_digest_parity` (run under the write lock at gc cadence, `heal_index`, and full-rebuild finalize) recomputes from a full scan and reseeds on mismatch — it heals drift but is NOT a substitute for calling `ensure_content_digest` in the rebuild migration. Tripwire tests: `schema_bootstrap_tests/content_digest.rs::{a_files_table_rebuild_drops_the_fold_triggers_and_ensure_recreates_them, a_files_write_without_the_fold_function_fails_closed}`. See [[#828 content_revision = MULTISET of (path,sha256) over ALL non-deleted main.files rows (overlays + staged gens included); XOR and counters are wrong]].

title: Node-auth (#881): symmetric hello order must break — dialer-first Auth, verify before ANY inventory/account bytes; mutual verification required
body:
Security review of the #881 node-auth design fixed these protocol requirements for the sync session:

1. The current symmetric session (both sides send Hello{account_id, have} concurrently) leaks the acceptor's account_id + full inventory hash set to an unverified dialer, and the dialer's to an impostor server. The authorized handshake must be sequential: dialer sends a small Auth frame (account_id + signed NodeBinding incl. device ed25519 pubkey) FIRST; acceptor verifies (scope, sig over domain-tagged canonical bytes, sha256(pubkey)==fingerprint, roster-effective in local fold, binding.node_pubkey == authenticated Connection::remote_node_id()) before sending ANY frame; then acceptor replies with its own Auth; dialer verifies it against remote_node_id (iroh guarantees this equals the dialed node id) BEFORE sending its inventory. Entry streaming stays concurrent after the auth exchange.
2. Mutual verification is required, not optional: it is what closes the poisoned-ticket hole (a dialer handed a hostile EndpointAddr would otherwise stream its whole signed account log to an impostor that claims an empty have-set).
3. Acceptor behavior pre-auth: do NOT call SyncStore::snapshot() before the binding verifies (currently run_session snapshots up front); use a short pre-auth first-frame timeout (seconds, not the 60s idle timeout — an unauthorized staller otherwise occupies the single-session accept slot); all pre-auth failures close uniformly (one generic error, no wrong-account vs not-on-roster vs bad-signature distinction — that distinction is an account-hosting oracle).
4. Admission class (Open/Closed/InviteToken) is local per-side, per-account config, never negotiated on the wire (a negotiated mode is a downgrade vector). Each side's class governs what IT reveals.
5. The NodeBinding canonical bytes must carry their own domain tag + version (device keys also sign account-log CBOR; without domain separation a binding could collide with an op preimage). Design the canonical statement once so a future persisted NodeBind account op (Design B) can embed the identical statement.
6. Do not bolt the binding onto the frozen Hello frame (arity-pinned decode); introduce the new handshake frame(s) and revise goldens/ALPN before any serve loop ships — after that the shape is compat-locked.

title: Table-sync anti-echo: apply records the row's synced hash ONLY when the op wins the row, so produce never re-emits a received row
body:
**Invariant (#893, whole-row LWW):** every apply that WINS a row records the row's synced-column hash into `sync_published_rows`, and `produce::produce_row_ops` emits an op only when the current row's hash differs. This stops the echo-republish loop: a row applied from a peer is recorded, so the next producer pass sees no delta and never re-signs/rebroadcasts it.

**The two halves:**
1. Only a WINNING op records the published hash. `apply_upsert` returns early (no published write) when the op loses the whole-row LWW (doesn't beat `sync_row_clocks`) — critical so a stale/losing op can't stamp an unsent LOCAL edit as published and make the producer drop it. A winning op replaces the whole row, then records the hash.
2. The hash is read back through the SAME path (`read_synced_cells`, mapping each column by its declared `ValueType`) the producer uses, so apply's recorded hash is byte-identical to what produce computes. It covers SYNCED columns only (`spec.columns`), never pk or `local_columns` — local re-resolution churn must never dirty it.

`produce_and_author` self-applies each authored op (which always wins, lamport = stream max+1) so the author's own row is recorded too (no self-echo). A `Remove` clears the published record.

**How to apply:** put re-derived/volatile columns in `TableSpec.local_columns`, never `columns`, so they stay out of the hash. Regression tests: `produce::tests::a_received_row_is_never_re_emitted`, `apply::tests::a_losing_upsert_does_not_publish_an_unsent_local_edit`, `engine::tests::...never_echoes`. See [[table-sync-removes-are-lww-ordered-via-sync-row-tombstones-order-independent-no-resurrection]].

title: Releases: release-plz cuts the tag + crates.io publish; cargo-dist owns the GitHub release + prebuilt binaries + npm publish (@rag-rat/bin)
body:
Since #550 the release pipeline is split between two tools; understand the handoff before touching `release-plz.toml`, `dist-workspace.toml`, or `.github/workflows/release.yml`.

**release-plz** (`.github/workflows/release-plz.yml`, `release-plz.toml`): bumps the lockstep version across the 3 crates, updates CHANGELOG.md, publishes all 3 to **crates.io**, and cuts exactly one `vX.Y.Z` git tag (only the `rag-rat` package has `git_tag_enable = true`). It does **NOT** create the GitHub release: `git_release_enable = false` on both `[workspace]` and the `rag-rat` `[[package]]`.

**cargo-dist** (`dist-workspace.toml` + generated `.github/workflows/release.yml`): the `vX.Y.Z` tag push (pattern `**[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+*`) triggers it to build prebuilt binaries for the 5 targets, generate installers (shell/powershell/npm), **create + publish the GitHub release** (`dist host --steps=create/upload/release`), and `npm publish --access public` the npm installer package (`publish-jobs = ["npm"]`, `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` ← the `NPM_TOKEN` repo secret).

**FOOTGUN (do not do):** never set `git_release_enable = true` on the `rag-rat` package in `release-plz.toml` — release-plz and cargo-dist would both try to create the same GitHub release and race.

**Two binary install channels:** `cargo install rag-rat` (crates.io, compiles from source, Rust toolchain) and `npx @rag-rat/bin` (prebuilt, no toolchain). `@rag-rat/bin` = `npm-scope = "@rag-rat"` + `npm-package = "bin"`.

**Constraints / how to apply:**
- cargo-dist `targets` MUST stay within ort's supported platforms — FastEmbed links ONNX Runtime statically via `ort-download-binaries`, so an unsupported target fails to build. Current set: aarch64/x86_64 apple-darwin, aarch64/x86_64 linux-gnu, x86_64 windows-msvc.
- Edit `dist-workspace.toml` then run `dist generate` to regenerate `.github/workflows/release.yml` — never hand-edit the generated workflow.
- Failure isolation: if the cargo-dist workflow fails, crates.io publish + the tag still happened (release-plz owns them), so `cargo install` is unaffected; only the GitHub release / prebuilt binaries / npm publish are at risk.
- This is phase 1 of the `@rag-rat/setup` milestone (#544); `@rag-rat/setup` (#545) builds on the `@rag-rat/bin` channel.

title: cargo-dist prebuilt binaries: the ort/ONNX-Runtime prebuilt forces per-target linker config (glibc image, dynamic CRT, no Intel Mac)
body:
rag-rat's embeddings pull in `ort` (fastembed feature), which at build time DOWNLOADS a prebuilt ONNX Runtime (`libort_sys`, from ort.pyke.io) and statically links it. That prebuilt's ABI + availability vary by target and fight cargo-dist's default build environment. The first cargo-dist release (v0.15.0) built ONLY aarch64-apple-darwin; the other four targets all failed to link `libort_sys`. Root cause is singular (the ONNX prebuilt), but the fix differs per platform — all in `dist-workspace.toml` (see PR #557):

- Linux (x86_64 + aarch64): dist builds on `ubuntu-22.04` (glibc 2.35), but the ONNX prebuilt references the C23 strtol family (`__isoc23_strtoll/strtoull/strtol`) added in glibc 2.38 → `undefined symbol` at link. FIX: pin the build image to glibc-2.39 via `[dist.github-custom-runners]` → `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu = "ubuntu-24.04"`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu = "ubuntu-24.04-arm"` (arm builds natively, not cross). No portability loss: the binary already required glibc ≥2.38 because it embeds that ONNX build.
- Windows (x86_64-pc-windows-msvc): needs TWO CRT fixes, both required together. (1) dist defaults to STATIC CRT (`+crt-static` → libcmt); the ONNX prebuilt is DYNAMIC (`/MD` → MSVCRT) → LNK2019 `__imp_tolower` etc. + LNK4098. FIX: `msvc-crt-static = false` (flips Rust's own objects to /MD). (2) That alone leaves `esaxx-rs` (C++ dep via tokenizers ← model2vec/fastembed), which HARDCODES cc `.static_crt(true)` → /MT, as the odd one out → LNK2038/LNK1319. FIX: force `CFLAGS=-MD`/`CXXFLAGS=-MD` on WINDOWS ONLY (cc appends env flags after its own /MT; cl.exe is last-flag-wins). Injected before `dist build` via `github-build-setup = "dist-build-setup/steps.yml"` (steps file in a workflows SUBDIR so GitHub doesn't parse it as a workflow). Mirrors the proven `.github/workflows/ci-cross-platform.yml` step. MUST stay Windows-gated: on macOS clang `-MD` means "emit make deps" and breaks the build.
- Intel Mac (x86_64-apple-darwin): `ort` ships NO prebuilt ONNX for this target/feature-set — hard block short of compiling ONNX from source. FIX: DROP the target. Apple Silicon (aarch64-apple-darwin) is the only Mac that links. Note bare `cargo install rag-rat` ALSO fails on Intel Mac (default features enable fastembed → ort → same missing target); the only source path is the pure-Rust embedder: `cargo install rag-rat --no-default-features --features model2vec`.

HOW TO APPLY: any new cargo-dist target must be one `ort` provides a prebuilt for AND satisfy the glibc/CRT constraints above. Don't re-add x86_64-apple-darwin without an ONNX-from-source build. dist-workspace.toml owns targets/runners/CRT/build-setup; release.yml resolves targets+runners at runtime from `dist plan`, so `dist generate` yields an identical workflow EXCEPT for trigger config (pr-run-mode, #555 set "skip") and github-build-setup steps (those ARE inlined into release.yml). The release build does NOT need ci-cross-platform.yml's `cargo clean -p ort-sys` — that was for rust-cache restore-key staleness; cargo-dist's build target isn't cached (only the `dist` binary is). ESCAPE HATCH: if ONNX linking ever becomes intolerable, switching the embedding backend to pure-Rust `tract` (ort's own error suggests `ort-tract`) removes all prebuilt-binary linking — every target builds from source, incl. Intel Mac — at a perf/op-support cost.

title: Cookbook Modal readiness is the endpoint serve-probe, NOT sb.waitUntilReady (which hangs on cold vLLM)
body:
**What:** The Modal recipe (`@rag-rat/cookbook` ≥ 0.8.1) resolves the tunnel first, then gates readiness ONLY on the endpoint HTTP serve-probe (`verifyChat`/`verifyEmbed`, which poll until a real completion/vector, tolerating connection-refused during boot). It no longer calls `sb.waitUntilReady()` and no longer sets a `readinessProbe: Probe.withTcp(...)` on `sandboxes.create`.

**Why:** On a COLD vLLM boot (esp. 30B FP8 on L40S), Modal JS SDK 0.9.0 `sb.waitUntilReady()` (the `sandboxWaitUntilReady` command-router RPC, gated on the TCP `readinessProbe`) HANGS INDEFINITELY even after uvicorn has bound `0.0.0.0:8000` and the encrypted tunnel already serves HTTP 200 — verified by curling the tunnel and by `modal.Sandbox.from_id(id).tunnels()` resolving instantly from Python while the JS wait was stuck 20+ min. The box bills the whole time and never emits `ready`; the provision subprocess stalls to the budget deadline and tears the box down with zero work. 0.9.0 is the newest Modal Labs SDK (the `modal` 1.x on npm are unrelated 2015 packages), so no version bump fixes it.

**How to apply:** Never reintroduce `sb.waitUntilReady()` as the readiness gate for a cold box. `sb.tunnels()` returns the tunnel URL as soon as it is allocated at creation (independent of the in-box server), so resolve it first and let the serve-probe be the sole readiness signal. Escape hatch if a box is stuck-but-serving: get its tunnel via the Python SDK (`modal.Sandbox.from_id(sbid).tunnels()`), point rag-rat at it in CONNECT mode (`[llm.*.remote] endpoint = <tunnel>`), and `sb.terminate()` when done.

title: Papertrail item and repo-comment progress are independent cursor lanes
body: Durable mirror progress must preserve every provider state dimension and validate a continuation before any page content or cursor state is committed. Item delta, backfill, item-comment, and repo-comment lanes checkpoint independently. GitHub REST item and repository-comment deltas walk updated timestamps ascending, but page-number continuations are mutable: a completed paginated scan may promote only the first page's inclusive maximum updated_at, because only that prefix is proven consumed. Item deltas persist item_delta_replay_required and clear the probe ETag until one complete overlapped verification walk sees the same frontier; a stable >100-row timestamp tie then settles and returns to conditional probes. Empty or raced list responses never advance to an unobserved probe timestamp. Repository-comment streams retain the same first-page candidate across pauses and promote it only after the stream completes. GitHub 404 is ambiguous between absent and inaccessible resources, so an item-comment 404 atomically unpins the active thread and keeps the last complete cached item/comments; successful full rewalk mark/sweep owns authoritative absence pruning. V063 checksum must change whenever its additive cursor shape changes so already-applied branch databases replay missing columns. GitHub historical backfill is a compound issue/pull-request Search cycle: each physical stream drains its first-page timestamp tie, and the next strict updated:< boundary is the newer (maximum) of the two stream boundaries. Pre-split SearchContinuation JSON remains a legacy combined stream and finishes without entering the split PR phase. Item comment refresh retains the previous complete set while pages arrive; paginated mutable walks require two identical complete ID sets before absence is accepted as deletion, and a process-level resume restarts the mark phase at page one. Full rewalk pruning, whole-table FTS rebuild, clearing full_rewalk, and last_full_sync persistence form one transaction. No special authority for the epoch-minting device; mint vs rotation differ in trigger, not authority. Gate per OP TYPE, not per log (a future member-self-scope DeviceName must not widen key_wrap's gate). HOW: no second authority evaluation — the secrets acceptance evaluator mirrors content/acceptance.rs and consumes the EXISTING control-projection fact queries: owner_secrets_authority (fold.rs, reads RosterFact/OwnerIncarnationFact secrets_boundary from DeviceRemove/OwnerDemote secrets_cut), stream_owner_effective, and auth_len_freshness LAST — all read in one snapshot inside refold_in_tx (storage.rs), same IMMEDIATE txn as rewrite_authority_projection, so a control refold retro-condemns wraps atomically (mirrors refold_streams_for_account). fold_account keeps folding ONLY log 0 (test a_known_op_on_a_non_control_log_is_not_folded — a DeviceAdd on log 1 mints nothing; keep that). title: Phase C membership model PROPOSAL (#405): account=principal, account-level grants, cut/prefix-freeze revocation, fold-indexed epochs — pending human freeze
body:
A designed-but-not-yet-frozen resolution of the #405 membership/revocation blockers (supersedes the sync-phase-c-design.md §4–§8 draft where they conflict). Key mechanisms, so the next agent doesn't re-derive them:

1. ACCOUNT = PRINCIPAL (person or org), a self-sovereign device roster with device roles owner/member. Streams are owned by one account; write/read access is granted account→account via StreamGrant{stream_id, grantee_account_id, role} in the OWNER's control log — never per foreign device. Multi-maintainer = org account with owner devices of several humans. Revocation levels: StreamRevoke (grant level, departures) vs DeviceRemove (device level, lost device, in the principal's own log).

2. REVOCATION = VALIDITY CUT (prefix freeze). Every remove/revoke op carries per-chain watermarks (seq, entry_hash) freezing the revoked party's chains to an exact hash-verified prefix. Below/at cut + ancestor-of-watermark-hash = valid forever (late delivery safe); beyond cut = condemned (quarantined, never deleted). Unlisted chains cut to empty; CutExtend (extend-only LWW register per chain) is the deliberate owner-mediated recovery for honest beyond-cut work. Back-dated forgery is impossible below the cut (would need a hash collision) and rejected above it regardless of claimed lamport. "The cut defines legitimacy"; "remove wins over concurrency".

3. EPOCH = FOLD-DERIVED INDEX, not authored: epoch N = state after the Nth EFFECTIVE control op in (lamport, device_fp, entry_hash) order. Header roster_epoch is an assertion/freshness hint only (fetch-before-fold when an entry asserts an epoch ahead of the local history — this is the truncated-relay/rollback mitigation). Fold output = epoch-indexed AccountAuthHistory (Vec<EpochRecord> with roster+grants+cuts snapshots, rejected list, condemned set); point-in-time authorization = binary search by order key.

4. FOLD = iterated-exclusion fixpoint: single ascending pass with authority-at-ordering-point, then condemn cut-violating entries (condemned set only grows → terminates ≤ n iterations, deterministic, pure function of the entry set). Over-condemnation is conservative and recoverable via CutExtend. Last-owner protection (WouldOrphanAccount), mutual owner-removal resolved by first-in-order-wins, removed fingerprints tombstoned forever (re-enroll = new key), effects attributed to the account (removing an owner does NOT cascade its past grants).

5. Forced contract changes: account envelope becomes 12 fields (lamport distinct from dense per-chain seq); the op-log entry envelope needs a /3 bump adding author_account_id + asserted epochs + crypto_suite/key_epoch, content chain key becomes (stream, account, device). Company forward-read revocation = StreamRevoke + key_epoch rotation wrapped only to remaining granted accounts' devices.

Judgment calls flagged for the human: org-as-account vs delegated admin grants; unlisted-chains-cut-to-empty; permanent fingerprint tombstones; conservative fixpoint; the 12-field header. Do NOT treat this memory as the frozen contract until the human confirms and the design doc is updated.

MINTING PRIMITIVES (`oplog/store.rs`), all take `&LocalDevice` (keeps `DeviceSecret`/`DevicePublic` `pub(super)`; `LocalDevice::fingerprint()` is `pub(crate)`, `secret()`/`public()` `pub(super)` — a `pub(crate)` accessor returning a `pub(super)` type trips `private_interfaces`):

The seam the wiring increment uses to make the table write + op-append ONE atomic unit (no nested txns). `author_op(conn,...)` = standalone wrapper.
- `author_genesis_in_tx(tx, stream, device, ops, now_ms) -> bool`: the GENESIS batch WITHIN a caller's txn — `assert_projector_not_newer`, GATE on empty chain (`chain_tail(tx,...).is_some()` → false), author all ops chained from genesis, ONE `reproject_after_write`, `stamp` — NO open/commit. `author_batch(conn,...)` = standalone wrapper (opens IMMEDIATE, delegates, commits; empty ops → false).
- Unlike `append` (foreign pre-signed entry, may Fork) these MINT a valid continuation from the tail, always Continuous under the single write-locked local writer. `append`'s reproject branch factored into shared `reproject_after_write(tx, stream)`.

LAYERING (avoids a cycle — do not violate): `oplog/mod.rs` gained its FIRST crate-internal API surface — curated `pub(crate) use` (`author_genesis_in_tx`, `chain_tail`, `local_device`, `owner_stream`, op vocab `EdgeSpec`/`MemoryOp`/`NodeContent`/`NodeId`/`NodeStatus`); `author_batch`/`author_op`/`author_in_tx` re-exported for completeness under `#[allow(unused_imports)]` (unconsumed until wiring). Every oplog submodule is otherwise PRIVATE. Translation + backfill live in `query/memory` (owns repo_memories/repo_node_edges), calling INTO oplog — ONE direction. NEVER add `oplog → query::memory`.

TRANSLATION (`authoring.rs::memory_to_ops`): row → `NodeCreate{content: NodeContent{kind,title,body,confidence,source,tags,payload}}`, then `NodeStatus{status}` ONLY when status != "active" — an UNKNOWN status token FAILS the backfill (not silently dropped to `active` in the SIGNED history), then an `EdgeAdd` per node-edge in `edge_key` order, DELIBERATELY no `Rebind`: the resolved dimension (`target_node_id`, `anchor_status`) is PER-DEVICE state recomputed on read by `reresolve_on_read` — signing it would bake one device's view into the immutable log (excluded for the SAME reason code-anchor BINDINGS are; the projection's `resolved_json` stays NULL for backfilled edges, recomputed locally on read).

title: Supply-chain gate: deny.toml + cargo-audit, and the cargo-deny v2 config gotchas
body:
The workspace has a supply-chain gate: `deny.toml` (repo root) + `.github/workflows/security.yml` running `cargo deny check` and `cargo audit` on dependency/policy-touching PRs & pushes plus a daily cron. (Added via the "add cargo-audit + cargo-deny" and "all-features clippy" PRs.)

Triage posture (how to respond when the gate goes red): vulnerabilities and unsound advisories must be FIXED — `cargo update -p <crate>` within semver to the patched version — never ignored. Only transitive `unmaintained` advisories with no upstream fix get `[advisories].ignore` entries, each with a `reason`. A new license shows up → review it, then add to `[licenses].allow` (or a scoped exception), don't widen blindly.

cargo-deny v2 config model (`version = 2`), empirically verified against cargo-deny 0.19.6 — these are NON-OBVIOUS and cost real investigation:

[advisories]
- `vulnerability`, `notice`, `severity-threshold` are DEPRECATED/removed under version=2 (using them → `error[deprecated]`). Vulnerabilities ALWAYS error — there is no vulnerability scope to set.
- `unsound` and `unmaintained` are advisory SCOPE enums: "all" | "workspace" | "transitive" | "none". They are NOT lint levels — `unsound = "deny"` is a PARSE ERROR (`unexpected-value`).
- Default `unsound` scope is "workspace", so a TRANSITIVE-only unsound advisory PASSES GREEN by default. Set `unsound = "all"` to fail on transitive unsound (verified: reverting memmap2 to 0.9.10 → `error[unsound]` only with `unsound = "all"`). Default `unmaintained` is "all".
- `yanked` IS a lint level ("deny"/"warn"/"allow").

[licenses]
- Dev- AND build-dependencies are EXCLUDED from the license check by default. Set `include-dev = true` and `include-build = true` to cover them (both are valid `[licenses]` keys). Proven to expand coverage (~67 more crates in this tree). NOTE: `cargo deny list` does NOT reflect `include-dev`; test coverage via `cargo deny check licenses` with a restrictive allow, not `list`.
- Prefer a per-crate `[[licenses.exceptions]]` (`crate = "..."`, `allow = [...]`) over a blanket `allow` entry for a narrow/weak-copyleft license, so a future crate with that license is forced through review. Here MPL-2.0 is scoped to `option-ext` this way rather than allowed workspace-wide.
- `[graph] all-features = true` so cargo-deny sees the full feature-gated dependency set (matches what `cargo audit` reads from Cargo.lock — e.g. feature-gated quinn-proto).

CLI gotcha: `cargo deny` does NOT accept `--config` BEFORE the subcommand (`cargo deny --config X check` → "unexpected argument"); it's `cargo deny check --config X`, or just run in the dir with `deny.toml`. cargo-deny DOES hard-error on unknown config keys (`error[unexpected-keys]` lists the valid set), so a typo'd field fails loudly rather than silently no-op'ing.

body: A workflow triggered only by `release: published` will not start when the release is created by `.github/workflows/release.yml` using the repository `GITHUB_TOKEN`; GitHub suppresses downstream workflow runs for events caused by that token. title: Dream churn-skip must invalidate on all 4 axes (body, inputs incl. dir-child files, prompt_version, uncitable terminal rows) or budget starves
body:
The dream verify/compact churn-skip predicate must invalidate on EVERY axis that changes what a stored verdict/summary means, AND every SURFACING reader must apply the SAME predicate the producer/queue uses — miss either and a stale row strands forever or shows obsolete data. (PR #428 review, six rounds.) verify.rs / verdict.rs / compact.rs / query/memory/hydrate.rs.

AXES (a stored memory_reality/memory_summaries row is CURRENT iff all match a fresh check):
1. content_hash — the NOTE content. `verify::note_content_hash(title, body)` = sha256 of trimmed title + "\n" + trimmed body (house memory_input_hash style; NOT a bare title‖body concat). Covers TITLE **and** body because BOTH the verdict prompt and the compaction prompt audit the whole note — a title-only edit re-verifies/re-summarizes and drops the stale verdict/summary/marker. (Renamed FROM `body_hash`; the memory_reality/memory_summaries column is `content_hash`, PK of memory_summaries is (repo_id, memory_id, content_hash). Do NOT reuse repo_memories.input_hash — it also folds kind+tags AND is FROZEN at creation: update_memory (api.rs) updates title/body in place with the SAME id but does NOT recompute input_hash.) queue reason enum is VerificationReason::ContentChanged.
2. checked_inputs_hash = the WHOLE evidence-pack fingerprint (column keeps this name). `verify::checked_inputs_hash` hashes sorted (path,sha) bound-file pairs `\u{1e}`-joined, `\u{1d}`, sorted (identifier,resolution) pairs. (a) bound files — resolve_bound_files expands a binding: empty path (`--dir .` root)→ALL files, dir→children via `path = ?1 OR path LIKE ?2 ESCAPE '\\'` with the dir LIKE-escaped (`_`/`%` are wildcards), file→itself; the (path,sha) MULTISET not bare shas; and it returns PATH-SORTED (not files.id rowid order) because bound_file_excerpts consumes THAT order under the MAX_EXCERPT_LINES cap — rowid order would let a reindex with the same (path,sha) set change which files land in the pack while churn-skipped. (b) identifier resolutions via identifier_resolution_pairs, EXACTLY as evidence_pack resolves. AMBIGUITY (both resolvers, same class): resolve_symbol returns ALL live defs of a bare name and resolve_file_segment returns ALL suffix matches of a shorthand path (both path-sorted; an exact file path is definitive/alone); resolve_identifier renders >1 as `symbols (N): …` / `files (N): …` instead of LIMIT-1-pinning to an unrelated namesake/same-suffix file — so the model never audits against a wrong match AND the churn key flips when any same-named/same-suffix match is added/removed (deleting the one the note meant re-verifies even if a namesake survives). An all-NOT_FOUND uncitable memory also re-queues once the code adds the symbol.
3. prompt_version — verdict `PROMPT_VERSION` / summary `COMPACT_PROMPT_VERSION` (pub(crate), re-exported through dream::mod as VERDICT_PROMPT_VERSION/COMPACT_PROMPT_VERSION). MUST gate EVERY reader: queue_reason (PromptChanged requeue), divergence_findings (SELECT+skip), hydrator summary (`AND prompt_version = COMPACT_PROMPT_VERSION`), hydrator marker (`AND prompt_version = VERDICT_PROMPT_VERSION`). Prompt heads live in dream/prompts/{verdict_head,compact_head}.md via include_str! (trimmed at render site); BUMP the matching *_PROMPT_VERSION when you edit a .md. Tests seeding these tables MUST stamp the current prompt_version.
4. UNCITABLE → a TERMINAL verdict-less row, not a requeue. `EvidencePack::is_citable()` = ≥1 excerpt OR ≥1 identifier that RESOLVED (!= NOT_FOUND). NOT_FOUND-only does NOT count (pass-0 unverifiable; counting it lets the model open a divergence citing NOT_FOUND, burning budget against the "unverifiable never asked of the model" contract). run_verdict_pass writes record_uncitable (NULL verdict, stamped content/inputs/prompt) so it churn-skips. Same starvation CLASS as anchor-broken: anything queued that can never write a row loops forever.

SURFACING STALE GATES = axes 1+2+3 at read time (SQLite has no sha256, so 1+2 recompute in Rust; hydrator needs the TITLE threaded from the caller). divergence_findings drops a `diverged` row unless prompt+content_hash+checked_inputs_hash all match current; hydrator (current_summary_and_verdict) drops the summary unless content_hash+compact prompt match and the marker unless content_hash(WHERE)+verdict prompt(WHERE)+evidence hash(Rust) match. A churn-SKIPPED but UNCHANGED memory keeps all axes matching so its finding/marker still surfaces (resolve-trap protection holds).

FABRICATION GUARD (verdict.rs verdict_is_cited + parse_verdict): an excerpt renders `path:line: <code>`, so `is_bare_locator` rejects a citation that is only `<path>:<digits>` with no text after. AND parse_verdict RESETS accumulated direction/evidence on each new `VERDICT:` line, so a scratchpad/`<think>` block's earlier VERDICT+EVIDENCE can't back-justify a different final verdict.

title: Created-dir watch placement must arm maintenance for extensionless directory events
body: `watch_created_dirs` cannot only install non-recursive watches; when it successfully places or refreshes target watches, the event loop must also debounce a maintenance pass. Created or moved directory events are extensionless, so `target_for_path` rejects them and normal base/linked relevance checks can be false even when the directory already contains indexable files (for example `mv pkg src/pkg` or a create event processed after `src/pkg/lib.rs` exists). The centralized helper therefore returns whether target watches were placed, and the event loop treats that as a pass request for both main and linked worktree overlays. When aggregating linked worktree states, do not use short-circuiting `any` for this side-effectful operation: visit every state and OR the result so multi-path events still update all applicable linked checkouts.
